batchName: Middle Republic: The Fall of Carthage and Corinth (167-133 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Middle Republic: The Fall of Carthage and Corinth (167-133 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What does Carthago delenda est mean?
questions.explanation: Cato has been credited with ending every speech with it, but the phrase is a later tradition.
questions.sourceQuote: with the words "Carthage must be destroyed" (*Carthago delenda est*).

questions.question: After the war, Carthage’s lands became the Roman provincia of Africa. Where was it governed from?
questions.explanation: Utica, a nearby port, had sided with Rome; the province became a major source of grain.
questions.sourceQuote: Carthage's lands became the Roman province (*provincia*) of Africa, governed from Utica

questions.question: How did Scipio Aemilianus celebrate the fall of Carthage?
options: With a triumphus, Rome’s victory parade
By founding a colony on the site
By building a temple to Eshmoun
questions.explanation: He also took the honorary surname Africanus, like his adoptive grandfather.
questions.sourceQuote: celebrated a triumph (*triumphus*), Rome's victory parade.

questions.question: Why did Scipio build a moles across Carthage’s harbour approach?
options: To stop supply ships getting into the city
To give his ships a safe harbour
To carry siege towers to the walls
questions.explanation: The Carthaginians answered by secretly digging a new channel to the sea.
questions.sourceQuote: Supply ships kept slipping into Carthage, so Scipio built a huge mole (*moles*), a stone barrier across the harbour approach.

questions.question: What happened to Carthage’s land after 146 BC?
options: It was confiscated as ager publicus, Roman public land
It was given to the Numidian king
It was shared among Scipio’s soldiers
It was returned to the survivors
questions.explanation: A curse was also laid on anyone who tried to resettle the site.
questions.sourceQuote: The land was confiscated as public land (*ager publicus*), the property of the Roman state.

questions.question: Which agnomen did Mummius take after destroying Corinth?
questions.explanation: Scipio Aemilianus took “Africanus” after Carthage, as his adoptive grandfather had.

questions.question: What did the lex Villia annalis set?
options: Minimum ages for offices: 41 for a consul
questions.explanation: In 147 BC the Senate suspended the age rules so that Scipio, 36 or 37, could be consul.
questions.sourceQuote: a law on minimum ages (*lex Villia annalis*) set the bar at 41.

questions.question: What was Scipio Aemilianus’s rank in the first years of the siege of Carthage?
questions.explanation: He saved Roman troops more than once, and visiting senators took note.
questions.sourceQuote: was serving as a military tribune (*tribunus militum*), a middle-ranking post.
